span: a person who has committed a serious crime and would ordinarily not be granted anticipatory bail
why: Illustrations about whether anticipatory bail can be sought while in custody in another case; seriousness is mentioned only in passing.

span: The imposition of conditions under Section 438(2) with reference to Section 437(3), in the opinion of this court, is enough safeguard for the authorities
why: Constitution Bench reasoning that conditions answer concerns such as the addition of more serious offences, so s.438 relief need not be withheld on that basis.

span: The grant of anticipatory bail in such a serious offence would operate to obstruct the investigation
why: Holding: anticipatory bail granted in a dowry-death case is set aside and bail cancelled because of the seriousness of the offence.

span: the High Court could not have stayed the investigations and restrained the investigating agencies from investigating into the cognizable offences
why: About stay of investigation under s.482 operating as a blanket no-arrest order; not about granting anticipatory bail for a serious offence.

span: The High Court, vide impugned order dated 19th December, 2022, granted anticipatory bail to Respondent No. 1
why: Recounts the High Court order and its reasons; the Supreme Court's own view is not in the passage.

span: the High Court has not at all considered the nature of allegations and the seriousness of the offences alleged against respondent No. 1
why: Court sets aside an anticipatory bail grant in a money-laundering case, saying the court must be very slow in exercising s.438 discretion for such economic offences.
